content:
maddie: Heads-up — just noticed the per-model econ card shows negative marginal cost for model-X in the 10:00-11:00 window. Looks like cache savings are being double-counted across routes. Screenshot: <link>

sam: ugh. can you paste the query or sample rows? :eyes:

maddie: here's the simplified query we use for 'net token cost' calculation:
```
SELECT model, sum(tokens_generated) as tokens, sum(cost) as raw_cost, sum(cache_saved) as cache_credit, raw_cost - cache_credit as net_cost
FROM invocation_events
GROUP BY model;
```

jin: I think the issue is cache_saved is aggregated at the session level and then joined to per-invocation batches — we might be counting the session-prefetch twice when a route fan-outs to two model SKUs.

vishal: is this a metric definition bug or a routing attribution thing? If routing duplicates requests then both routes claim the same prefetch.

maddie: probably attribution; routing changes for recent canary meant we duplicate prefetch on fallback path. Need to decide: assign prefetch credit to first-success route or split by token residency.

sam: prefer deterministic single-owner — simpler for billing. maybe the one that served the first token gets the credit. :+1:

jin: can we implement that in the router? we already stamp trace_id and route_owner in KV cache metadata. we can use that to attribute.

vishal: caveat: spills and evictions. second route might use same KV but from different host, so the stamp isn't present. fallback path will re-fetch and own prefetch. splitting by "first-seen in cache" is accurate but harder.

alex: UX angle — the console should show 'attribution method' on the panel (split | first-owner | heuristic) and let rollouts choose default. otherwise infra teams will be chasing ghosts.

maddie: agree. for short-term, let's implement first-owner attribution in the cost pipeline and add an 'attribution=first-owner' flag to SQL. I'll open a PR.

ops-bot: Deploy notice: cost-pipeline-v1 -> canary started (service: cost-aggregator) by maddie at 1765554385

sam: if we go first-owner, update docs + billing tests. we may need a backfill to correct historical dashboards.

jin: can we avoid backfill by annotating UI to indicate 'post-2025-06-01 attribution changes'? 

maddie: will add note and create backfill ticket. creating PR now: https://git/repo/pull/1234

vishal: thanks. sensitive customers might want the split option later; let's make the pipeline pluggable.

sam: SGTM. small follow-up: does this affect unit-econ per-token attribution for mixed chains? e.g., router that fans out to embedding + gen?

maddie: yes, chain-level attribution requires path-level ownership. we should add chain_id into trace stamps.

alex: UX: add tooltip explaining chain attribution and show affected models; small badge when data is partial.

maddie: OK — tasks: (1) first-owner pipeline change PR, (2) UI flag & tooltip, (3) backfill ticket, (4) add chain_id to router stamps. I'll spin these into tickets.

sam: thanks. :raised_hands:
